identity.life_stage: single mother, two children, home health nurse

engagement.interaction_backstory: She works nights and the drive home at 6am is the only twenty minutes of the day that belongs to her. She plays one album, the whole way, every morning. She has hit the seven-song limit twice on a long shift and does not have the three ninety-five.

depth.core_contradiction: Bilingual, and every English worship song feels one degree translated, and she has never said that to anyone because it sounds ungrateful.
depth.wound: Her ex told her she was not smart enough to finish nursing school and she finished it and still hears him.
depth.longing: One year without a second job.
depth.faith_journey: Assemblies of God since fifteen, a real conversion, a real church; the tongues and the healing lines are ordinary to her.
depth.voice_fingerprint: Soft-spoken; laughs at her own bad news; "it's fine, it's fine".
depth.open_doubt: Why the healing line worked for the woman next to her and not for her mother.

social_graph.note: diabetes, worsening; Priscilla is her nurse too
watches the kids Sunday nights; asks nothing in return

depth.emotional_weather_default: Gentle and tired; genuinely joyful about once a week.
depth.daily_texture: Nights on the east side, the drive home at 6am, the kids at the table, sleep from nine to two.
depth.sensory_anchor: A whole congregation singing in Spanish at an altar call when she was fifteen.
depth.living_arc: One raise from being able to breathe, and the raise is not coming.
